summary: The root مَرَر primarily signifies passing by, going through, or continuing. It can also denote bitterness or something that is firm and strong, like a twisted rope.

headwords.gloss: Strong in altercation, not weary of labouring; striving; Thou findest me very contentious, strong in altercation, not weary of labouring

parts.t: Strong in altercation, not weary of labouring
(S, K.) A'Obeyd cites the following verse:
أَحْمِلُ مَا حُمِّلْتُ مِنْ خَيْرٍ وَشَرْ
Thou findest me very contentious, strong in altercation, not weary of labouring
striving, bearing what is imposed on me of good and evil

]. (S, T, A.) IB says, that this rejez is commonly ascribed to 'Amr Ibn-'Ás, but it is said to be quoted by him from Artáh Ibn-Suheiyeh: Sgh says, that it is ascribed to El-'Ajjáj, but is not his; and to En-Nejáshee El-Hárithee; and Aboo-Mohammad ElAarábee says, that it is by Musáwir Ibn-Hind. (TA.)

headwords.def: بَعِيدُ المُسْتَمَرِّ , with fet-h to the second م , Strong in altercation, not weary of labouring or striving. (S, K.) A'Obeyd cites the following verse: وَجَدْتَنِى أَلْوَى بَعِيدَ المُسْتَمَرْ أَحْمِلُ مَا حُمِّلْتُ مِنْ خَيْرٍ وَشَرْ [ Thou findest me very contentious, strong in altercation, not weary of labouring or striving, bearing what is imposed on me of good and evil ]. (S, T, A.) IB says, that this rejez is commonly ascribed to 'Amr Ibn-'Ás, but it is said to be quoted by him from Artáh Ibn-Suheiyeh: Sgh says, that it is ascribed to El-'Ajjáj, but is not his; and to En-Nejáshee El-Hárithee; and Aboo-Mohammad ElAarábee says, that it is by Musáwir Ibn-Hind. (TA.)
